1.title: Defender for Endpoint: Advanced Features, Rules and Custom Data Collection
1.text: Welcome to Module two: Defender for Endpoint: Advanced Features, Rules and Custom Data Collection. It covers the exam area one. Manage a security operations environment. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Configure Microsoft Defender for Endpoint advanced features. Configure rules settings in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. Configure custom data collection in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: one. Manage a security operations environment (forty to forty-five percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft S C-two hundred study guide and Microsoft Learn.

1.title: Advanced features
1.text: Advanced features. Path: Settings, then Endpoints, then General, then Advanced features. Set a feature On or Off, then Save preferences. The exam picks the feature that fits a stated need.

1.title: Advanced features, continued
1.text: Advanced features. The figure shows this: Where the Defender for Endpoint settings live.

1.title: Advanced features, continued
1.text: Advanced features. Enable E D R in block mode. Blocks malicious artifacts even when Defender Antivirus is in passive mode. Automatically resolve alerts. Resolves alerts with no threats or remediated threats; does not overwrite alerts you set to In progress or Resolved. Configure allow or block file settings. Lets you allow or block files with indicators; needs Defender Antivirus active and cloud-delivered protection. Configure custom network indicators. Allow or block I P s, U R Ls and domains; needs Windows ten seventeen oh nine or later, or Windows eleven.

1.title: Advanced features, continued
1.text: Advanced features. Enable tamper protection. Stops attackers from turning off security features. Restrict correlation to within scoped device groups. Stops incident merging across device groups; affects future correlations only. Enable live response and live response for servers. Allows live response sessions (Module thirteen). Allow unsigned script execution in live response. Lets unsigned Power Shell scripts run in a session. Configure automatic attack disruption. Turns on automatic attack disruption (Module four). Exam tip: E D R in block mode equals Defender Antivirus is passive (for example a third-party antivirus is primary). Allow or block file equals indicators and needs active antivirus and cloud protection.

1.title: More advanced features to recognize
1.text: More advanced features to recognize. Hide potential duplicate device records. On by default; tenant-wide. Download quarantined files. On by default; needed to download a quarantined file. Configure web content filtering. Needs a web content filtering policy. Enable user details display. Shows Microsoft Entra user details in the alert queue and device page. Enable the unified audit log. Writes Defender activity to the unified audit log. Enable device discovery. Finds unmanaged devices on the network. Share endpoint alerts with Microsoft Compliance Center. Feeds Purview solutions such as insider risk.

1.title: More advanced features to recognize, continued
1.text: More advanced features to recognize. Configure the Microsoft In tune connection. Must be turned on in both In tune and Defender for Endpoint. Configure Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps integration. Connects endpoint signals to Cloud Apps. Enable authenticated telemetry and Enable preview features. Authenticated sensor data; early access to new features. Configure Endpoint Attack Notifications. Direct notifications from Microsoft Threat Experts.

1.title: Indicators
1.text: Indicators. Indicators let you allow, audit, warn or block an entity. They are managed under the Rules area of Settings, then Endpoints. Files. Allow, Audit, Warn, Block execution, Block and remediate. I P addresses. Allow, Audit, Warn, Block execution. U R Ls and domains. Allow, Audit, Warn, Block execution. Certificates. Allow, Block and remediate.

1.title: Indicators, continued
1.text: Indicators. Limit: fifteen thousand indicators per tenant; it cannot be increased. The old action alert only is now Audit; alert and block is now Block and remediate. When several controls apply, the order is: application control (W D A C, App Locker), then Defender Antivirus exclusions, then block or warn file indicators, then Smart Screen, then allow file indicators, then A S R, controlled folder access and antivirus. Exam tip: Certificates have only two actions: Allow and Block and remediate. Files have five.

1.title: Other rules under Settings, Endpoints
1.text: Other rules under Settings, Endpoints. Alert suppression. Hides alerts that match a rule (Module one). Indicators. Allow, audit, warn or block files, I P s, U R Ls and certificates. Custom data collection. Collects extra telemetry into Sentinel (next section). Isolation exclusions, automation uploads and automation folder exclusions. Exceptions for device isolation and for automated investigation file handling.

1.title: Custom data collection
1.text: Custom data collection. Custom data collection collects extra endpoint telemetry beyond the defaults and sends it to Microsoft Sentinel for hunting. A rule filters on folder paths, process names or network connections. Open. Settings, then Endpoints, then Rules, then Custom Data Collection. First. Select the Sentinel workspace (top right), even if it is already connected. Wizard. General Information, Create rule (table, action, conditions), Define rule scope, Review and finish, Submit. Scope. All applicable client devices, or devices with dynamic tags. Manage. Edit, Enable checkbox, Delete (permanent; history stays in Sentinel).

1.title: Custom data collection, continued
1.text: Custom data collection. Data lands in five tables: Device Custom Process Events, Device Custom Image Load Events, Device Custom File Events, Device Custom Network Events and Device Custom Script Events. License. Defender for Endpoint Plan two. Sentinel. One workspace per tenant. Tags. Dynamic tags only (manual tags are not supported), set in Asset Rule Management and run at least once. Clients. Windows ten or eleven at the minimum client version; Windows Server twenty nineteen or later. Volume cap. seventy-five thousand events per device per rule per twenty-four-hour rolling window; collection for that rule then stops until the window resets. Delay. Deployment typically takes twenty minutes to one hour. Exam tip: Custom data collection needs Plan two, a Sentinel workspace and dynamic tags. The seventy-five thousand events per device per rule per day cap is the likely numeric question.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A company uses a third-party antivirus as primary, so Defender Antivirus runs in passive mode. The sock still wants malicious artifacts blocked after a breach. Which advanced feature should be enabled? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Enable E D R in block mode for all onboarded devices. E D R in block mode blocks malicious artifacts even when Defender Antivirus is passive.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. An engineer creates a file indicator to block a hash, but the block never takes effect. Which two conditions must be met for the feature to work? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Defender Antivirus is active and cloud-delivered protection is on. Allow or block file settings need active antivirus and cloud-delivered protection.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A sock needs an indicator type that offers only the actions Allow and Block and remediate. Which type is it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Certificates, which offer only two possible actions. Certificate indicators support only Allow and Block and remediate.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A threat hunter needs extra file events from a specific folder on Windows eleven clients, stored in Sentinel. Which table receives the data from a custom data collection rule? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Device Custom File Events, one of five custom tables. File-based rules write to Device Custom File Events.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A custom data collection rule stops sending events from one busy server before the end of the day. What is the most likely reason? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The rule reached its cap of seventy-five thousand events per device in twenty-four hours. The cap is seventy-five thousand events per device per rule per twenty-four-hour rolling window.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A company with two device groups does not want incidents to combine devices from different groups. Which advanced feature meets the requirement? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Restrict correlation to within scoped device groups. The feature stops incident merging across device groups for future correlations.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Where are the advanced features of Defender for Endpoint configured? Answer: Settings, then Endpoints, then General, then Advanced features. Question two. What is the maximum number of indicators per tenant? Answer: fifteen thousand. Question three. Which two actions does a certificate indicator support? Answer: Allow and Block and remediate.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which license does custom data collection need? Answer: Defender for Endpoint Plan two. Question five. What is the new name of the old "alert only" indicator action? Answer: Audit. Question six. Which tables receive custom data collection events? Answer: Device Custom Process Events, Image Load Events, File Events, Network Events and Script Events.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Advanced features: Settings, then Endpoints, then General, then Advanced features. Passive antivirus: E D R in block mode. Allow or block files: active antivirus and cloud-delivered protection. Indicators: files five actions, I P s and U R Ls four, certificates two; fifteen thousand per tenant. Custom data collection: Plan two, Sentinel workspace, dynamic tags, five Device Custom tables. Cap: seventy-five thousand events per device per rule per twenty-four hours.
